text: Gentlemen. The robot cast a portal to the Nether, lit it, and walked through. On the very spot where it once stood still for thirty-nine minutes.
Problem one. Lava. The robot kept picking the lava under the lake, the one it could never reach. So it stood by the pool, replanning, for minutes. Now it takes the lava on top.

Problem two. A shaft. It once stood in one cell for twelve minutes, retrying the same route every tick. Now, if a site cannot be reached, it gives up and moves on. We taught it to quit. We are very proud.
Same save. Lava buckets: none out of three before, two out of three after. Out of the shaft: two runs out of two. The lava lake course passes.
And then it reached the Nether. It arrived next to a sea of lava, and went for a swim. The lab boys are calling it a successful one-way trip.
Version zero point nine five point six zero. Out now. The Nether is next week's problem.
